milestones.label: Cast
milestones.title: Character designs
milestones.summary: Static designs of the whole cast (24 figures), all generated against the same Matt image as the style anchor and one shared proportion rule, cut out and forced to greyscale (only Inéz's lipstick is red). For sprite animation in Ludo.ai later.

milestones.label: M0
milestones.title: Pipeline tests
milestones.summary: Can we make art, voice and music and get them into the game as files? Yes for all three. Art now comes from Gemini.

samples.title: Lineup: minor cast

samples.title: Proportion check: same eye height
samples.about: Every character scaled so the distance from eyes to floor is identical (yellow line), so head size, torso and leg length can be compared directly. After this check, Natalia, Corrigan, Sol, Hartley, Stefan, Inéz, Kate and Zofia were regenerated with one shared rule: about 7.5 heads tall, the same head-to-body ratio and leg length as Matt, with heavier or older builds shown only by width, posture and clothes.
lookFor: Does anyone still look out of proportion next to the others?

samples.title: Matt Long
samples.about: Matt Long, 37, private investigator and ex-NYPD detective. Tall, lean, a little stooped with tiredness. Rumpled grey single-breasted three-piece suit, white shirt, loosened dark tie, a fedora with a dented crown, two-day stubble, tired sharp eyes, square jaw. Hands relaxed at his sides.
lookFor: Right for the character? Face, age, build, clothes, 1930 period.

samples.title: Pete Duckerton
samples.about: Pete Duckerton, about 35, crime reporter. Boyish face with an eager grin, slim build, average height. Fedora pushed back on his head with a press card tucked in the hatband, rumpled striped suit, long knitted scarf hanging untied round his neck, a rolled-up newspaper in one hand, the other hand in his trouser pocket.
lookFor: Right for the character? Face, age, build, clothes, 1930 period.

samples.title: Kate Duckerton

samples.title: Natalia Long (née Kowalska)

lookFor: Right for the character? Face, age, build, clothes, 1930 period.

samples.title: Matt as a cut-out puppet (v8, walk matched to Muybridge)
samples.about: Skinned mesh with a motion system. The walk is now tuned against Eadweard Muybridge's 1887 photographs of a man walking (Animal Locomotion, plate 1): steps of about 0.41 x his height, the front heel landing well ahead of the hip, a push-off up on the toes of about 58°, the swing foot trailing high behind before it comes through, a forward lean of about 6° with the gaze slightly down, and fuller elbow bend on the forward arm. Footprints are placed in advance and legs are solved hip-to-ankle, so the planted foot cannot slide and the body never moves backwards. Idle, Gesture and Reach keep the feet planted; switching animations blends.
lookFor: Walk: does it read as a man walking now? Compare with the Muybridge samples.
Pace: one stride every 1.15 s. Slower and wearier for Matt?
Known: side view only; the far leg is a darker copy of the near one.

samples.title: Walk vs Muybridge: 12 frames
samples.about: Top: Eadweard Muybridge, Animal Locomotion plate 1 (1887), a man walking, 12 consecutive frames covering just under one stride (public domain; Wellcome Collection). Bottom: Matt rendered at the same moments of his stride.
lookFor: Leg spread at contact (frames 3 and 10), the trailing back foot after push-off (4-5), the passing pose (7).
Muybridge's walker is unclothed and barefoot; Matt's jacket and shoes change the silhouette, not the mechanics.

samples.title: Walk vs Muybridge: key poses
samples.about: The four key poses of a walk, Muybridge left and Matt right in each pair: contact (frame 3), push-off (5), passing (7), contact on the other leg (10).
lookFor: Do Matt's legs, lean and arms match the photograph in each pair?

samples.title: Matt's proportions and joints
samples.about: Blue lines: where each joint sits on an average adult man, as a fraction of height from the floor (Drillis & Contini). Yellow ticks: head heights; Matt is 7.3 heads tall (crown hidden under the hat, worked out from eyes and chin). Red dots: the rig's joints. Before this check the shoulder was 56 px and the elbow 50 px too low (about 2.5% of his height), the ankle 46 px too high and the knee 15 px low; all now sit on the standard lines, and the neck pivot moved from the front of the collar to the middle of the neck.
lookFor: Do the dots sit where you'd expect the joints under the suit?
Is 7.3 heads the right build for Matt, or should he be leaner and taller?

samples.title: Matt's puppet pieces
samples.about: Every piece of the puppet on its own: head, torso with shoulder socket and natural hem, near upper arm, forearm and elbow patch, far upper arm and forearm (palm side), thigh, shin with shoe, knee patch. Patches are soft-edged discs that sit over the joints. The far leg reuses the near leg, darkened.
lookFor: Any leftover background, clothing on the head, or ragged edges?

samples.title: Matt: reference and three poses
samples.about: Left: the first reference (Gemini added an overcoat). Then three poses generated with that reference attached: side profile, walking, talking.
lookFor: Is this Matt? Face, build, age, the dented fedora.
Overcoat as his outdoor look, or suit only?
Painted look and lighting: right for the game?

samples.title: Parts sheet for the puppet
samples.about: One generation asked for every body part separately. Head and armless torso came out exactly right; arms and legs were a mix of whole limbs and halves.
lookFor: Nothing to approve here yet; this shows where the puppet pieces come from.

samples.line: Love letter from the landlord. He always writes when the money's late.

samples.title: Period music: King Oliver, "Tears"
samples.about: King Oliver's Creole Jazz Band, recorded October 1923, with Louis Armstrong on second cornet. Public domain in the US. From the George Blood 78rpm transfers at the Internet Archive.

Right energy for Doyers Street?
